 Order

09.05.2025 Heard Mr. B.U. Laskar, learned counsel for the petitioner; Mr. R. Boro, learned counsel representing Mr. C. Baruah, learned Standing Counsel, NHAI and NHIDCL for the respondent nos.
1, 7 & 8; Ms. N. Bordoloi, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue & Disaster Management Department for the respondent nos. 2 & 3; and Mr. S.S. Roy, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam for the respondent nos. 4, 5 & 6.
2.

The case of the petitioner is that a plot of land measuring 2 Bighas, covered by Dag no. 195 &
Periodic Patta no. 11, situate at Village - Nohmali, Pargona - Katigorah, Mouza - Nohoma, District - Cachar, Assam ['the subject-plot', for short] came to be acquired by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways [MoRT&H], Government of India [GoI].
The initiation of the land acquisition process was by a Notification dated 05.01.2023 under Section 3A[1] of the National Highways Act, 1956 ['the N.H. Act', for short].
Thereafter, the compensation amounts towards land acquisition and zirat were assessed by the Competent Authority Land Acquisition [CALA] [the respondent no. 5].
3. The petitioner is claiming a share in the compensation amount assessed under Section 3G[1] of the N.H. Act in respect of the subject-plot, which has been quantified at Rs. 25,25,832/-.
The petitioner is claiming to be an occupier of the subject-plot.
Prima facie, the petitioner is not a landowner of the subject-plot.

4. From the Communication dated 19.02.2024 [Annexure-B to the writ petition], it transpires that the said compensation amount is contemplated for disbursement of the compensation amount in favour of the respondent no. 9.
From the statements and averments made in this writ petition, it prima facie transpires that neither the petitioner nor the respondent no. 9 is the landowner of the subject-plot.
Rather, one Abdul Mnnan is the patta holder of the subject-plot.
Page No.# 4/4 5.
Thus, the Court is of the considered view that the matter would require further examination.
6. Issue notice, returnable in 6 [six] weeks.

7. As Mr. Boro, learned counsel has appeared and accepted notices on behalf of the respondent nos.
1, 7 & 8; Ms. Bordoloi, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue & Disaster Management Department has appeared and accepted notices on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 & 3; and Mr. Roy, learned Junior Government Advocate, Assam has appeared and accepted notices on behalf of the respondent nos.
4, 5 & 6, issuance of formal notice to the said respondents stands dispensed with.

The learned counsel for the petitioner shall furnish requisite nos. of extra copies of the writ petition along with the annexures, to the learned counsel for the respondents within 2 [two] working days from today.

9. List the case after 6 [six] weeks.
